thread:
Alex: quick pass this morning on Triton-style JIT costs + kernel-cache churn on g5.2x.
Alex: summary up front: cold compile on new kernel shapes is the dominant source of tail latency for long seqs. saw ~200ms per-kernel compile in the sample set.
Maria: can you share the capture + exact nsys command?
Alex: uploaded artifacts to s3://redwood-perf/triton-jit/1799123345/ and perfetto URL: https://ui.perfetto.dev/trace/XYZpqR9
Alex: nsys I ran (single profile):
``nnsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --output=triton_jit_1799123345.nsys-rep --sample=cpu --stats=true --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx``
Ryan: do we have a breakdown host-compile vs enqueue vs device-exec? previous traces were ambiguous.
Alex: extracted timeline shows host compile ~55% of the observed 260ms cold spike; kernel enqueue/launch ~30%; kernel device execution ~15%.
Tanya: that ratio screams JIT overhead. How many unique kernel compile keys per request?
Alex: roughly 5-8 unique attention kernels per request when seq_len mixes 512/1024/1536. small differences in tile/block cause separate compiles.
Maria: KV cache interplay? does kv cache eviction drive more variants?
Alex: yes. mixed single-turn and multi-turn workloads evict compact kernels. observed kernel_cache_miss ~0.72 on trace sample; cache size looked constrained (<128 entries) with LRU churn.
perf-bot: automated parse -> kernel_cache_miss=0.72, avg_compile_ms=195, median_kernel_launch_ms=12, total_span_ms=268
Ryan: 195ms per compile is huge. is that one kernel or aggregate?
Alex: per-kernel on cold path. cache-hit path measured ~6-12ms end-to-end.
Tanya: proposal A: emit fewer, more general kernel variants that cover adjacent seq_len buckets (accept slight perf loss on narrow case) to reduce distinct compile keys.
Ryan: proposal B: async compilation + fallback path: first request uses generic fallback kernel while host compiles optimized kernel asynchronously and swaps in for later requests.
Maria: we need microbench harness to validate perf regressions if we broaden patterns. don't land heuristics without numbers.
Alex: sketched two experiments:
  1) enlarge kernel cache to 1024 entries and replay perfetto to map miss vs cache size.
  2) implement async-compile fallback POC that serves generic kernel + background compile.
Alex: experiment scripts in s3://redwood-perf/triton-jit/1799123345/experiments/
Tanya: add NVTX around compile start/finish and increment counters for cache hits/misses in runtime telemetry. we need production signal, not just traces.
perf-bot: suggested alerts/dashboards: metric triton_compile_ms_p95 > 120ms or kernel_cache_miss_rate > 0.25 -> page / ticket.
Maria: who owns the async-compile POC?
Ryan: I'll take async-compile POC and instrument NVTX. aiming for branch + baseline by EOD Friday.
Alex: I'll run cache-size A/B and replay traces with varied cache limits to measure miss curve and memory impact.
Tanya: I'll create tickets PERF-3421 (async compile POC), PERF-3422 (cache-size A/B), PERF-3423 (telemetry NVTX + metrics) and tag eng-runtime + infra.
Ryan: one more idea: batching rule to avoid mixing very different seq_lens in same batch. small heuristic: group by seq_len bucket with >80% similarity or cap batch to avoid combining 512 and 1536. Add as feature flag.
Maria: good, add to PERF-3422 as an optional toggle for AB testing. include repro steps and links to perfetto/nsys artifacts.
Alex: will add README in s3 experiments with exact commands to reproduce the runs.
perf-bot: noted owners -> Ryan (PERF-3421), Alex (PERF-3422), Tanya (PERF-3423). next check-in requested in ticket comments.
Maria: thanks all. please post short summary in the ticket once POCs land.
Alex: posting follow-up benchmarks tonight and will attach updated perfetto nsight captures.
Tanya: assigning follow-ups for eng-runtime + eng-infra to ensure telemetry pipelines can ingest new counters.
